summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded C programming and RTOS experience across STM32 and Jetson-class platforms. Built bare-metal firmware and FreeRTOS-based device driver development spanning microcontroller internals, GPIO/ADC/I2C peripherals, and concurrent, mutex-protected task scheduling, debugging on real hardware with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers. Comfortable working the full embedded stack, applying data structures and algorithm design from interrupt-driven peripheral drivers up through sensor-to-actuator control loops and systems-level integration debugging.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometer peripherals with a Raspberry Pi over I2C and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.

Designed a custom tap-detection algorithm in embedded C using z-axis differential thresholding — an exercise in algorithm design over raw sensor peripherals; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built embedded C firmware for an STM32 Cortex-M4 microcontroller with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C device driver, programming GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, and I2C1 peripherals directly in bare-metal C.
Achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified timing and signal behavior in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM device drivers with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Ran FreeRTOS with mutexes for concurrent, shared-memory task scheduling and coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) across a distributed embedded pipeline through systematic hardware-software debugging; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on an embedded Arduino microcontroller in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection via I2C-multiplexed dual VL53L0X ToF sensors.
Deployed the Jetson-side control bridge as a systemd service with auto-restart and non-root isolation, plus static IP networking, for reliable multi-device bring-up and communication.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
